name: rbac
description: Fine-grained role-based access control layered on top of Cognito groups: roles, permissions, role<->permission grants, user<->role assignments, and a check_permission API for policy enforcement.
author: Biffo Team

columns.name: name
columns.description: Role slug, e.g. 'viewer', 'system.admin'. Roles prefixed 'system.' cannot be deleted (application-enforced; see README).

columns.name: is_system
columns.description: True for built-in roles that cannot be deleted. Nullable because the generic create route has no server-side default (see README's 'declared defaults are not enforced' note) -- treat NULL as false. The plugin itself always sets this explicitly when seeding roles.

columns.name: effect
columns.description: 'allow' or 'deny'. Nullable for the same reason as rbac_roles.is_system -- NULL is treated as 'allow' by the plugin's check_permission logic.

columns.name: role_id
columns.description: References rbac_roles.id. PluginTableDefinition (issue #18) has no foreign-key concept -- this is a plain column enforced only at the application layer, not a DB constraint.

columns.name: permission_id
columns.description: References rbac_permissions.id (application-enforced, no DB foreign key -- see role_id note).

indexes.name: idx_rbac_role_permissions_unique_pair
indexes.description: Stands in for the issue's original 'PRIMARY KEY (role_id, permission_id)' -- PluginTableDefinition always injects its own synthetic 'id' primary key (see README), so a second composite primary key isn't possible; a unique index over the pair is the closest supported equivalent and is enforced identically at the database level.

columns.name: user_id
columns.description: References users.cognito_sub (application-enforced, no DB foreign key -- see rbac_role_permissions.role_id note).

columns.name: role_id
columns.description: References rbac_roles.id (application-enforced, no DB foreign key).

columns.name: assigned_by
columns.description: cognito_sub of the admin who made the assignment, or NULL for system-assigned rows (e.g. the default-role auto-assignment on user.created).

columns.name: expires_at
columns.description: Optional expiry for temporary elevated access; NULL means the assignment never expires.

api_routes.description: List all roles for the caller's tenant.
Delete a role. Generic CRUD cannot enforce 'system roles can't be deleted' -- that rule is application-level only (see README).
List role->permission grants. Not present in the issue's original route table -- added because check_permission has no data to evaluate without a way to grant permissions to roles.
Grant a permission to a role.
Revoke a permission from a role, by the grant row's own id.
Assign a role to a user.

Remove a role assignment, by the assignment row's own id. The issue's original design was 'DELETE /rbac/assignments' identified by a user_id/role_id body -- issue #19's RouteDefinition requires single-row delete operations to address a row via an {id} path parameter, so this deletes by the assignment row's own id instead.

event_subscriptions.description: Auto-assigns the default 'viewer' role to newly created users. Informational only -- Core API route registration (issue #19) only reads 'tables' and 'api_routes' from this manifest; event subscriptions are wired in the plugin's own Lambda (src/rbac/main.py) via the SDK's EventSubscriber, not synthesized by the Core API. Core publishes user.created from routers/auth.py when a User row is first created on first login (ADR-0010), so this subscription is live once the plugin is installed.
